units.title: Domain A: Introduction and Overview of Clinical Aesthetic Health Sciences

outcomes.text: Define aesthetic health sciences and explain how it improves appearance, supports mental well-being and links healthcare with beauty.
Identify current trends: non-invasive treatments, personalised skincare and social media influence.
Identify career paths such as aesthetician, skincare specialist and laser technician.
Describe the duties of aesthetic professionals: skin analysis, treatments and skincare advice.
Understand basic skincare principles: skin types and concerns, product ingredients, routines and habits.

units.title: Domain B: Anatomy, Physiology, and Skin Health

outcomes.text: Explain the basic structure of the skin: epidermis, dermis, hypodermis.
Describe the main functions of the skin: protection, regulation and sensation.
Identify skin appendages: sweat glands, sebaceous glands, hair and nails, and what each does.

units.title: Domain C: Hygiene, Sterilization, and Infection Control

outcomes.text: Explain why sterilisation prevents infection by reducing transmission and keeping a clean environment.
Identify sterilisation tools and their use: autoclaves, disinfectants, UV light.
Follow safety and sanitation rules in practicals: wear PPE, clean and disinfect surfaces.
Apply personal hygiene: wash hands often, keep nails short and clean, wear clean clothes.
Identify sterilisation and disinfection methods: autoclaving, chemical, UV.

units.title: Domain D: Skin Types, Conditions, and Professional Consultation

outcomes.text: Identify and group skin types: normal, dry, oily, combination, sensitive.
Assess skin condition by looking at texture and tone and identifying concerns and goals.
Recommend suitable products and treatments by understanding the client's skin and giving personal advice.
Understand basic products for different skin types: cleansers, moisturisers, sunscreens.
Choose products for individual skin types and concerns, using ingredient knowledge.
Run a basic consultation by asking relevant questions and giving personalised recommendations.
Understand basic skin anatomy and physiology: structure and function.
Understand how to keep skin healthy through prevention and protection.

units.title: Domain E: Skin Care, Facial Preparation, and Product Application

outcomes.text: Recognise internal factors affecting skin health: genetics, nutrition, hydration.
Recognise external factors: pollution, UV radiation, lifestyle choices, product use.
Understand why regular facial treatments help, for different skin types and individual needs.
Learn guidelines for safe product use: follow instructions, use moderately, patch test new products.
Show patch test procedure: spot allergens or irritants and run the test safely.
Maintain healthy skin by adjusting product use to feedback, protecting from stressors, and managing stress and hormonal change.

units.title: Domain F: Skin Maintenance and Personalized Skincare Planning

outcomes.text: Create a basic AM/PM routine for the client's skin type.
Explain the purpose of toners, moisturisers and sunscreens.
Show basic application techniques for daily products.
Identify your skin type and understand its needs.
Select basic products suited to individual skin types.
Develop a long-term plan for healthy skin and specific concerns.

units.title: Domain G: Non-Invasive and Device-Based Aesthetic Procedures

outcomes.text: Set up lab equipment and tools for practical work.
Apply learned techniques in real or simulated client sessions.
Show a professional attitude and manner in the practicum lab.
Learn the standards and protocols for aesthetic practice.
Show attention to detail and commitment to quality in services.
Do a basic visual skin analysis on a clean face using light.
Follow proper sanitation and hygiene in the lab.
Develop basic communication skills for working with clients.

units.title: Domain H: Advanced Facial Techniques and Hydra Facial Procedures

outcomes.text: Show basic manual and scrub exfoliation.
Apply basic hydration techniques with suitable products.
Sanitise workstations and tools by basic sterilisation protocol.
Identify and wear basic PPE (mask, gloves) with clients.
Record basic treatment details accurately in the client file.

units.title: Domain I: Client Handling, Professional Ethics, and Record Management

outcomes.text: Keep high standards of personal hygiene and appearance.
Identify roles within a salon hierarchy.
Respect clients' personal space and preferences.
Receive and act on feedback from teachers or peers.
Understand why sanitising tools and personal hygiene matter.
Follow guidelines keeping both clients and yourself safe.

units.title: Domain J: Clinical Practicum and Laboratory Skills

outcomes.text: Set up lab equipment and tools for practical demonstrations.
Apply learned techniques in real or simulated client sessions.
Show a professional attitude and manner in the practicum lab.
Learn the standards and protocols for aesthetic practice.
Show attention to detail and commitment to quality.
Do a basic visual skin analysis on a clean face using light.
Follow proper sanitisation and hygiene in the lab.
Develop basic communication skills with clients.

units.title: Domain K: Final Skills Appraisal, Portfolio, and Research

outcomes.text: Compile a portfolio of completed practical activities.
Show proficiency in basic facial techniques.
Present a portfolio showing practical work and experience.
Record basic client data and treatment notes.
Analyse simple aesthetic cases and draft basic treatment plans.
Show professionalism and ethics in client interactions.
Understand basic marketing principles for aesthetic services.

units.title: Domain A: Introduction and Overview of Clinical Aesthetic Health Sciences

outcomes.text: Understand the scope of practice, separating non-invasive treatments from minimally invasive ones.
Explain the limits and risks of aesthetic practice and why training and licensure matter.
Do basic skin analysis: determine skin type and spot concerns like acne and hyperpigmentation.
Stay current through workshops, industry publications and professional networking.

units.title: Domain B: Anatomy, Physiology, and Skin Health

outcomes.text: Describe the functions of skin layers: epidermal barrier, dermal collagen and elastin, and hypodermis fat storage.
Explain how lifestyle, medication, UV exposure, stress and health disorders affect skin.
Explain how pollution, climate and UV radiation affect skin health.
Describe strategies for healthy skin: routines, sun protection, lifestyle changes.

units.title: Domain C: Hygiene, Sterilization, and Infection Control

outcomes.text: Use and handle autoclaves correctly: loading, temperature and pressure, maintenance.
Use UV sterilisers correctly: exposure time and distance, surface preparation, limits and safety.
Repeat of UV steriliser use: exposure time, surface preparation, limitations and safety.
Use and dispose of single-use instruments properly, including handling and storage.
Apply infection control: chain of infection, standard precautions, transmission-based precautions.

outcomes.text: Understand causes, symptoms and treatments of acne vulgaris: pathophysiology, topical and systemic treatment, contraindications.
Identify and manage pigmentation disorders such as melasma and hyperpigmentation.
Understand causes and consequences of skin sensitivity and barrier function disorders, including irritant contact dermatitis.
Distinguish dehydrated skin from dry skin by causes and symptoms.
Understand advanced skincare ingredients such as retinoids, peptides and growth factors, and recommend products and treatments for specific concerns.

units.title: Domain E: Skin Care, Facial Preparation, and Product Application

outcomes.text: Explain benefits of active ingredients such as salicylic acid, hyaluronic acid and vitamin C.

Select products for individual concerns such as acne-prone, aging or sensitive skin.
Demonstrate advanced product use: layering and combining products.
Understand interactions between skincare products and other products or medications.
Optimise skincare routines for individual skin types and goals.
Educate clients or peers on product use, benefits and interactions.
Analyse skincare trends and product claims, weighing science, benefits and drawbacks.

units.title: Domain F: Skin Maintenance and Personalized Skincare Planning

outcomes.text: Develop a customised AM/PM routine for individual concerns.
Apply products well: layering order, right amount, frequency by skin type.
Explain benefits of anti-aging products, exfoliants and brightening agents.
Customise product choice by concerns, needs and goals.
Adjust routines when skin type, concerns or environment change.
Understand interactions between skincare and other products or medications.
Choose sunscreen by skin type, concerns and activity, and understand SPF and broad-spectrum protection.

units.title: Domain A: Introduction and Overview of Clinical Aesthetic Health Sciences

outcomes.text: Define clinical aesthetics and tell it apart from general beauty care.
Explain its role in modern skincare and health industries.
Identify main application areas: rejuvenation, acne, pigmentation and anti-aging.
Distinguish cosmetic from clinical treatments by technique, products and expected outcomes.
Describe ancient beauty and skincare practices (Egyptian, Greek, Roman).
Identify key innovations such as lasers and chemical peels.
Discuss the move from traditional beauty practices to science-based treatments.
Identify roles: clinical aesthetician, laser technician, medical spa therapist, specialist, educator, business owner.
Explain the qualifications, training and skills each career path needs.

units.title: Domain B: Anatomy, Physiology, and Skin Health

outcomes.text: Identify the layers of skin and explain their functions.
Recognise skin cells (keratinocytes, melanocytes, Langerhans, Merkel) and their roles.
Analyse histological slides to identify skin layers and structures.
Distinguish thin from thick skin.
Understand how skin protects against UV radiation, pathogens and dehydration.
Describe skin regeneration and wound healing.
Understand common skin disorders such as acne and eczema.
Explain the causes of these conditions at cellular and molecular levels.
Learn how skin flora protect against pathogens.
Describe the effect of bacterial, viral and fungal infections on skin.

units.title: Domain C: Hygiene, Sterilization, and Infection Control

outcomes.text: Define basic hygiene principles: hand hygiene, personal cleanliness and environmental sanitation.
Understand hygiene's role in preventing infectious disease spread.
Show proper personal hygiene: bathing, oral hygiene, handwashing.
Explain the importance of hygiene in homes, schools and public spaces.
Link poor hygiene with disease transmission, such as foodborne and respiratory infections.

units.title: Domain D: Skin Types, Conditions, and Professional Consultation

outcomes.text: Describe the basic structure and function of the skin's three layers.
Identify skin types and common conditions such as acne, eczema and rosacea.
Do basic skin health assessments, spotting dehydration or early aging.
Run a skin consultation and give personalised recommendations from individual needs.
Give basic skincare recommendations covering daily routine, sunscreen and hydration.

units.title: Domain E: Skin Care, Facial Preparation, and Product Application

outcomes.text: Describe basic face anatomy and skin types for tailoring facial treatments.
Follow skin preparation steps: cleansing, exfoliating, toning.
Identify facial products (cleansers, masks, serums, moisturisers) and select them by skin type and condition.
Perform intermediate facial steps: massage, masks and hydration.
Recommend personalised routines and aftercare based on skin type and the facial given.

units.title: Domain F: Skin Maintenance and Personalized Skincare Planning

outcomes.text: Identify daily routine components: cleansing, moisturising and sun protection by skin type.
Choose cleansers, toners, moisturisers and sunscreens by skin type and condition.
Understand how facials and peels address acne, dryness and uneven tone.
Create personalised daily routines for acne, aging or dryness.
Educate clients on routines, products and post-treatment aftercare.

units.title: Domain G: Non-Invasive and Device-Based Aesthetic Procedures

outcomes.text: Use device-based procedures such as microdermabrasion, LED therapy and facial steamers, and their purposes.
Explain how devices work, e.g. microdermabrasion exfoliates and LED light stimulates collagen.
Follow basic safety protocols with devices: skin preparation, handling, post-procedure care.
Assess client suitability for device treatments by skin type and condition.
Give post-treatment advice such as avoiding sun and using gentle products.

units.title: Domain H: Advanced Facial Techniques and Hydra Facial Procedures

outcomes.text: Discuss deep cleansing facials, enzyme peels and multi-step exfoliation.
Apply facial massage to relax, boost circulation and improve texture.
Explain skin types and choose suitable facial techniques for each.
Apply hydrating, exfoliating and anti-aging masks by skin need.
Give pre-treatment preparation and aftercare advice to maximise benefit and limit risk.

units.title: Domain I: Client Handling, Professional Ethics, and Record Management

outcomes.text: Understand why client confidentiality and privacy matter.
Show ethical behaviour with clients, respecting rights, dignity and consent.
Keep accurate, up-to-date client records, including history and product use.
Get informed consent so clients understand the procedures.
Maintain professional boundaries for respectful relationships.

units.title: Domain J: Clinical Practicum and Laboratory Skills

outcomes.text: Greet and talk with patients in a clinical setting: introduce yourself, explain treatment, keep them comfortable.
Take vital signs under supervision (blood pressure, temperature, pulse, respiration) and record them.
Prepare patients for basic skin treatments, such as cleansing and toning before a facial.
Document patient information, history and observations accurately and confidentially.
Follow infection control: sanitise equipment, prepare treatment areas, use PPE.

units.title: Domain K: Final Skills Appraisal, Portfolio, and Research

outcomes.text: Create a portfolio with consultation notes, before-and-after photos and evidence of skills.
Collect client feedback, reflect on performance and summarise how it shaped practice.
Track and document outcomes of at least three treatments, covering techniques, satisfaction and changes over time.
Research a skincare product, document its benefits and application, and demonstrate it clinically.

units.title: Domain A: Introduction and Overview of Clinical Aesthetic Health Sciences

outcomes.text: List basic clinical aesthetic treatments: facials, microdermabrasion, chemical peels, laser treatments.
Describe the purpose and benefits of each treatment.
Recognise contraindications and side effects, and consultation protocols before treatment.
Show professional behaviour and client communication techniques.
Understand how communication, ethics and professionalism shape client satisfaction.
Identify the latest trends and technologies in clinical aesthetics, such as LED therapy and hydrafacials.

units.title: Domain B: Anatomy, Physiology, and Skin Health

outcomes.text: Examine and compare detailed histological features of skin.
Analyse tissue samples for abnormalities such as melanoma or basal cell carcinoma.
Evaluate the clinical relevance of histological findings.
Explore how histology guides treatments such as laser therapy, topical medication and grafts.
Investigate the pathophysiology of skin cancer, dermatitis and vitiligo.
Discuss genetic, environmental and immune factors in skin disorders.
Apply knowledge of skin structure and disorders to clinical scenarios such as diagnosing conditions or suggesting treatments.
Examine the principles of anti-aging treatments and their effect on skin cells.
Understand ways to protect skin from environmental damage, including sunscreen, clothing and lifestyle.
Study how nutrition and hydration affect skin health.
Discuss advances in dermatology: stem cell therapy, gene therapy and nanotechnology.

units.title: Domain C: Hygiene, Sterilization, and Infection Control

outcomes.text: Explain advanced hygiene protocols in clinical, food and public health settings.
Understand hygiene's effect on community health and strategies to control epidemics.
Demonstrate hygiene and sanitation protocols in healthcare, including hand hygiene and equipment sterilisation.
Understand how hygiene prevents nosocomial infections and outbreaks in healthcare facilities.
Analyse hygiene in global health, disaster management, refugee camps and large-scale disease control.

units.title: Domain D: Skin Types, Conditions, and Professional Consultation

outcomes.text: Understand advanced analysis methods such as skin analysers and digital imaging.
Identify complex conditions such as hyperpigmentation, acne scars, rosacea and skin cancer risk.
Run detailed consultations considering environment, lifestyle and nutrition.
Design customised skincare routines from skin condition, lifestyle and age.
Recommend and discuss advanced cosmetic treatments such as peels, microdermabrasion and laser.

units.title: Domain E: Skin Care, Facial Preparation, and Product Application

outcomes.text: Show advanced understanding of facial anatomy and conditions for targeted treatments.
Perform advanced preparation: professional exfoliation such as enzyme peels, hydration and toning.
Evaluate professional-grade products and customise selection by skin, age and lifestyle.
Perform advanced facial techniques: advanced massage, masks, and tools such as steamers or LED therapy.
Give in-depth custom routines and aftercare considering long-term skin health and treatment history.

units.title: Domain F: Skin Maintenance and Personalized Skincare Planning

outcomes.text: Design advanced daily routines with specialised products for anti-aging, acne and hyperpigmentation.
Fit clinical treatments (peels, microdermabrasion, LED) into plans targeting specific issues.
Create clinical plans combining daily routines and professional treatments for lasting results.
Evaluate and select serums, masks and exfoliants to complement clinical treatments.
Educate clients about routines and clinical treatments with aftercare and lifestyle advice.

units.title: Domain G: Non-Invasive and Device-Based Aesthetic Procedures

outcomes.text: Learn advanced devices: RF skin tightening, ultrasound therapy, micro needling, and their clinical uses.
Understand device mechanisms, e.g. how RF tightens skin and micro needling boosts collagen.
Hold detailed consultations for device procedures, assessing skin, history and expectations.
Operate devices competently, know settings, and maintain equipment and hygiene.
Recognise and manage risks such as irritation, burns and pigmentation change.
Give detailed aftercare covering side effects, products and recovery timeline.

units.title: Domain H: Advanced Facial Techniques and Hydra Facial Procedures

outcomes.text: Use jade rollers, gua sha or high-frequency devices to improve tone and texture.
Design facials targeting acne, hyperpigmentation, fine lines and dullness.
Apply professional facial protocols from cleansing to masks, step by step.
Customise facials to the client's skin condition, lifestyle and concerns.
Consult thoroughly, then recommend and perform the most suitable facial.
Give advanced aftercare with professional-grade products and lifestyle changes.

units.title: Domain I: Client Handling, Professional Ethics, and Record Management

outcomes.text: Understand legal requirements for protecting client personal and health data.
Apply ethical decision-making frameworks to client care situations.
Keep detailed, secure client records: treatment plans, progress notes, post-care instructions.
Explain client rights and responsibilities, including refusing treatment and following aftercare.
Show professionalism that respects cultural differences, individual needs and non-discrimination.
Learn the legal and ethical implications of record keeping, such as GDPR or HIPAA compliance.

units.title: Domain J: Clinical Practicum and Laboratory Skills

outcomes.text: Conduct a full skin analysis, identifying skin types and conditions, and record findings for treatment planning.
Assist, under supervision, in advanced treatments such as peels, microdermabrasion or LED therapy.
Perform advanced facial techniques (masks, massage, exfoliation) while monitoring patient comfort.
Record detailed histories, treatment protocols, progress notes and post-treatment care.
Work with other clinicians to create and carry out treatment plans.
Give post-treatment care instructions on sun protection, hydration and product use.

units.title: Domain K: Final Skills Appraisal, Portfolio, and Research

outcomes.text: Compile a full portfolio including consultations, outcomes, team contributions and extra certifications.
Write clinical case studies from your own treatments of different skin types and conditions.
Analyse a treatment you repeated for effectiveness and propose improvements from feedback and results.
Present a hands-on demonstration of a new skincare device, with how it works, benefits and safety.
Run a practical research project applying a skincare treatment to clients with different skin conditions and document results.
